theBigPicture: Hurricane Isaias slammed into the Gulf Coast and is now drenching the Southeast, leaving hundreds of thousands of homes without power from Florida to the Carolinas. At the same time, President Trump's surprise deal to buy diesel from Russia is drawing fire as fuel prices sit near wartime highs, and missile attacks near Riyadh keep the Middle East conflict boiling. In short: your lights, your fuel bill, and the world's biggest flashpoints are all in play this week.

householdImpact.energyAndFuel: Crude oil is still carrying a 'war premium' — Brent crude sits around $125 a barrel — which keeps gas pump prices elevated, and the new US deal to import Russian diesel is an attempt to bring trucking and heating fuel costs down, though relief won't show up overnight. Natural gas prices are normal, so home heating and cooking bills should stay steady for now.
householdImpact.borrowingAndMortgages: Financial markets are calm and credit is flowing easily, so mortgage and auto loan rates should hold roughly steady rather than jump. Credit card rates remain high, making this a good moment to pay down balances before the holiday spending season.
householdImpact.groceriesAndSupplyChain: Diesel — the fuel that moves trucks, trains, and food — is expensive because of the war premium, and those costs eventually show up at the grocery checkout. Separately, the FDA is weighing a rule that would let more food additives skip safety review, so label-reading shoppers may want to stay alert.
householdImpact.jobsAndSavings: With stock markets calm and borrowing conditions easy, 401(k)s and retirement accounts should be stable this week, with fuel-driven inflation the main risk to watch. The November 3 midterm elections could shift policies on taxes and jobs, and markets tend to react to the outcome.

globalFlashpoints.summary: A Russian glide bomb destroyed an apartment block in Zaporizhzhia, killing at least 15 people including children, while Ukraine warns the US diesel deal with Putin will simply fund more such attacks.

Houthi missile attacks are pulling Saudi Arabia directly into the wider Iran conflict, including a deadly strike near Riyadh's airport, even as Putin relays Iran's position on a possible peace deal to Trump.
No major new military tensions in the region over the past day, leaving trade and shipping as the main things to watch rather than any immediate confrontation.

India's youth-led protests against the election chief and PM Modi brought massive police deployments and hundreds of detentions in Delhi, while US airport security workers are pushing back against new on-the-job rules as midterm campaigning heats up.

topStories.headline: Hurricane Isaias knocks out power to hundreds of thousands across the Southeast
topStories.whyItMatters: The storm has been downgraded, but flooding and 'spinoff tornadoes' remain a threat from Florida up through the Carolinas. If you're in the storm's path, expect possible outages and closed roads for days while utility crews work to restore power.

topStories.headline: Trump strikes diesel deal with Putin — and Ukraine says it will bankroll the war
topStories.whyItMatters: The White House is turning to Russia for diesel despite sanctions as US fuel prices sit near wartime highs ahead of the midterms. Critics, including Ukraine's president, warn the money will fund Russia's attacks — like the strike that just killed 15 people in Zaporizhzhia.

topStories.headline: Saudi Arabia enters the danger zone as Houthi attacks escalate
topStories.whyItMatters: A deadly attack near Riyadh's airport shows the Iran conflict is now directly touching the world's biggest oil exporter. Every escalation ripples through energy markets — and eventually your gas pump.

topStories.headline: FDA may let toxic chemicals slip into food without safety review
topStories.whyItMatters: The regulator wants to expand a loophole allowing some hazardous additives into food as long as they aren't known to cause cancer. Shoppers could see more unreviewed chemicals on ingredient lists if the change goes through.

topStories.headline: India detains protest leaders as youth anger boils over in Delhi
topStories.whyItMatters: Tens of thousands of police were deployed and hundreds detained ahead of demonstrations against the election chief and PM Modi. Unrest in the world's most populous country can rattle markets and disrupt supply chains far beyond its borders.

topStories.headline: America's November 3 midterms could make history for women candidates
topStories.whyItMatters: Control of Congress and key governorships is on the ballot, with real consequences for taxes, healthcare, and energy prices. Mortgage rates and stock markets often move on the results.

whatWeAreWatching: Isaias's remnants: flood watches and wind advisories stretch into the Carolinas — watch power restoration numbers and road closures over the next 48 hours.
Whether the Russian diesel deal actually translates into cheaper fuel at the pump — and how Ukraine, Congress, and US refiners respond.
Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and any sign of a Trump-brokered Iran peace framework after Putin relayed Tehran's position.
The November 3 US midterm elections, with fuel prices and the cost of living front and center in the final stretch.
Whether India's protest crackdown escalates or de-escalates after this weekend's mass detentions in Delhi.
